title: District Factorization of Minimum-Cost Reusable Intervention Menus for Causal Transport Identification
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The original content is a collection of narrow extensions of established hedge-and-hull design machinery.
The primal-width algorithm is a generic CSP compilation, and the unique-triple vertex-cover gadget tightens an existing hardness construction rather than establishing a broader tractability frontier.
The factor-k menu-versus-trial comparison is valid for nonnegative additive prices, but exact equality uses zero-price auxiliary capabilities and strictly positive instances only approach the factor.
Derive a sharp graph-dependent refinement of the factor-k menu-versus-trial bound and match it with causal constructions under normalized strictly positive prices.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved and source-attested the ordinary-hedge menu formulation, full-bidirected-component factorization, effective-scope enumeration, the nonnegative-price factor-k comparison, and restricted algorithmic and vertex-cover consequences. The field claim collapsed at D0.5 because these results remain a specialized extension of established hedge/hull and CSP machinery; the only plausible field upgrade is a new graph-dependent strictly-positive-price frontier, which requires a D-1.2 re-anchor.
tldr: The reusable-menu problem separates exactly across active full bidirected districts without a width assumption: every required kernel depends only on its controllable hull scope, and the global extended-real optimum is the sum of component optima. Writing \(R_{\Delta}=\bigcup_{i\in I_{\Delta}}R_i\), exact local enumeration uses \(\sum_{\Delta}2^{|R_{\Delta}|}|I_{\Delta}|\) candidate hull tests after scope construction and the full-menu precheck. The formal bounded-scope premise \(|R_{\Delta}|\le2\) gives at most four component candidates, each checked against every assigned kernel, and at most \(4k\) candidate tests. The separate condition \(|L_{\Delta}|\le2\) remains unchanged and is only an easily inspected sufficient condition because \(R_{\Delta}\subseteq L_{\Delta}\). The restricted causal vertex-cover construction shows that simple blockers without this component-scope separation remain globally hard.
gap: Existing causal-effect design work supplies districtwise hedge criteria, hull oracles, additive and nonadditive family costs, SAT/ILP formulations, single-district hardness, and an exact size-two-minimal-hedge regime for one kernel. It does not give a primitive original-ADMG condition under which one reusable purchase vector for arbitrarily many required kernels decomposes into independently and exactly solvable infrastructure modules.
fill: Prove that the full-menu hull precheck exactly detects infeasibility, that every hedge and its blocker remain in one full bidirected district, that the two-lever condition implies rank-two nonempty blockers, and that nonnegative menu cost separates componentwise. Establish the boundary with the explicit unique-three-vertex-hedge vertex-cover realization, and retain the sharp all-\(k\) reuse construction as the value-of-infrastructure theorem while treating generic rank-two cover recovery, hull locality, and primal-width compilation as corollaries or supporting machinery.
